title: A Study on Reflective Reciprocal Peer Coaching for Pre-service Teachers: Change in Reflectivity
venue: Journal of Education and Training Studies
extended_summary:
This study examines whether a reflective reciprocal peer coaching (RRPC) program can improve the reflectivity of pre-service teachers. The central question is whether training on RRPC and participation in the RRPC process lead to measurable changes in how pre-service teachers think about and reflect on their teaching, moving them from technical reflection toward contextual and dialectical reflection.

The intervention involved 12 pre-service English language teaching teachers at a Turkish university during their field experience course. Participants first received 12 weeks of training on reflection, RRPC, observation forms, and reflective diary keeping, followed by 8 weeks of peer coaching practice in triads at state schools. Each cycle used pre-conference, observation, and post-conference discussion, with structured observation tools and video-based intervention sessions to support analysis. Quantitative data came from the Profile of Reflective Thinking Attributes administered three times, and qualitative data came from reflective diaries, video recordings of post-conference sessions, and focus-group interviews.

Findings showed statistically significant gains in reflectivity after training and again after RRPC practice. Descriptively, participants shifted from mostly technical and contextual reflection to more contextual and dialectical reflection by the end of the study. Qualitative evidence suggested that participants increasingly focused on student needs, rationale for teaching decisions, and ethical dimensions of classroom practice. The author concludes that reflective reciprocal peer coaching, when paired with training and structured support, can foster deeper reflective practice in pre-service teacher education.

identified_tools.name: CAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Collaborative peer coaching / reflective coaching model where teachers observe each other, give structured feedback, and reflect on teaching practice.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper studied reflective reciprocal peer coaching (RRPC) for pre-service teachers, including training, observation forms, pre-conferences, post-conferences, reflective diaries, and focus-group interviews to examine changes in reflectivity.

findings.finding_summary: In a mixed-method study with 12 Turkish ELT pre-service teachers, reflectivity scores on The Profile of Reflective Thinking Attributes increased significantly after RRPC training and again after RRPC practice. Wilcoxon signed-rank tests showed significant pre-post differences after training (z=-3.061, p=.002) and after practice (z=-3.065, p=.002), and the distribution shifted from 6 technical/6 contextual/0 dialectical at baseline to 0 technical/5 contextual/7 dialectical after practice.
findings.measure: The Profile of Reflective Thinking Attributes; reflective diaries; post-conference recordings; focus-group interviews

quality_tier_rationale: This is a mixed-methods peer coaching study, not an evaluation of an AI tool or generative coaching system. The evidence is qualitative/mixed-method and focused on reflective practice, so it is not a high-causal-inference AI study.
impact_tier_rationale: No AI system was studied, and no effect size was reported. While the reflective coaching intervention showed positive changes in reflectivity, the paper does not support an AI tool impact estimate.
